Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 89, verses 1–5:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Fajr (The Dawn), because it opens with Allah's oath by the time of dawn.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Presenting to the idolaters of Makkah, in their turning away from accepting the message of their Lord, the example of the nations that denied their messengers before them, such as ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of Pharaoh, and explaining what punishment befell them because of their transgression. Implicit in this is the affirmation of the Prophet (ﷺ), together with the promise of destruction for his enemies.

• Explaining Allah the Exalted's sunnah (way) in testing His servants in this life with good and evil, and nullifying the delusion of the idolaters of Makkah, who reckoned that the bounties they enjoyed were a sign that Allah had honored them, and so they neglected to thank Allah for that.

• Mentioning the Hereafter, its terrors and its hardships, the division of people on the Day of Resurrection into the blessed and the wretched, and explaining the end of the wicked soul and the noble, virtuous soul.

[Al-Tafsir]

Allah the Exalted swears by the time of dawn, by the ten nights at the beginning of Dhul-Hijjah and what they have been honored with, by every even and odd, and by the night when it passes on with its darkness. Is there not, in the oaths mentioned, a sufficient deterrent for one of understanding?

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 89, verse 15:

As for man, when his Lord tests him with blessing, extends his provision, and gives him the finest of living, he thinks that this is because of his honour before his Lord, so he says: "My Lord has honoured me."
As for when He tests him by restricting his provision, he thinks that this is because of his humiliation before God, and so he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."

Not so! The matter is not as this human being supposes. Rather, honor lies in obedience to God, and humiliation in disobeying Him. But you do not honor the orphan, whose father has died while he was young, nor do you treat him kindly. Nor do you urge one another to feed the needy, who has no means to suffice for himself and meet his need. You devour the rights of others in inheritance with greedy devouring, and you love wealth with excessive love.
